name: AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit
author: WPAssist

sections.description:
AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit is an all-in-one WordPress optimization toolkit designed to improve website performance, strengthen security, simplify administration, and streamline website maintenance.

Unlike plugins that focus on a single area, AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit combines performance enhancements, security hardening, maintenance tools, and administrative controls into one easy-to-use plugin.

Whether you’re a website owner, freelancer, agency, or WordPress maintenance provider, AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit helps you build faster, cleaner, and more secure WordPress websites.

Diagnostics Centre

Run read-only checks that help explain whether important WordPress systems are configured and operating as expected.

WordPress and Site Address configuration
HTTPS and search engine visibility
Environment and debug configuration
REST API and loopback requests
WordPress.org and outbound HTTP communication
Background updates and scheduled events
WP-Cron configuration and recorded update failures
Focused Scheduled Task Health summary
Page cache and persistent object cache
PHP memory limit
WordPress memory limits
Database server version
Maximum upload and POST sizes
Maximum execution time, input time, and input variables

AssistKit distinguishes informational configurations from actual problems. Different frontend and WordPress addresses, disabled visitor-triggered WP-Cron, and hidden search visibility are not automatically treated as failures when they may be intentional.

CRON and Scheduled Task Health

Monitor WP-Cron events and Action Scheduler queues from a dedicated CRON screen without sorting through a raw list of technical hooks.

Detect when the site-wide WP-Cron runner appears stalled, including sites that use an external server cron
Identify overdue recurring events and distinguish a runner-wide problem from individual task concerns
Detect repeated Scheduled Action failures from the last seven days
Detect stalled and substantially overdue Scheduled Actions
Identify high-confidence duplicate WP-Cron schedules and Scheduled Actions
Show task ownership evidence for WordPress core, installed plugins, shared frameworks, and other identifiable sources
Allow for valid plugins that register some cron callbacks only when work is required
Run a lightweight callback and schedule health observation automatically once per day
Observe callback-free events across three separate automatic checks before identifying them as likely leftovers
Continue monitoring every day after the initial three checks so newly abandoned tasks can still be discovered
Offer guarded leftover-event removal with best-effort undo when the available evidence meets the required confidence threshold
Delete selected failed Action Scheduler history or cancel selected stalled, overdue, and duplicate actions
Keep WordPress core tasks and active conditional plugin tasks protected from inappropriate removal
Hide healthy tasks by default while providing a collapsed read-only reference table of existing tasks
Reflect detected Scheduled Task Health problems in the Diagnostics Centre summary

Database Optimization

Manage database retention and cleanup from one full-width panel with settings that save automatically.

Configure post revision, trash, and auto-draft retention
Choose which WordPress cleanup tasks run manually or on the daily schedule
Remove expired transients, spam comments, and orphaned metadata
Clear a stale pre-WordPress 6.4 directory-size transient when it has no valid expiration
Optimize database tables after cleanup
Clean expired WooCommerce customer sessions and transients when WooCommerce tables are present
Remove orphaned WooCommerce order items, item metadata, HPOS addresses, and HPOS operational data using conservative parent checks
Clean completed and canceled Scheduled Actions older than 15 days
Optionally remove failed Scheduled Actions older than 60 days
Remove orphaned Scheduled Action logs
Run the saved cleanup selections immediately or schedule them once per day

Autoloaded Options Manager

Review the largest non-protected options WordPress loads automatically and identify settings that may be adding unnecessary database overhead.

View total, manageable, and protected autoloaded option sizes
Review the top 20 manageable autoloaded options by size
Check up to 50 large options against installed plugin, MU-plugin, and theme code, including safely constructed option prefixes
Recognize additional option families from WPCode, Divi, The Events Calendar, Event Tickets, GiveWP, WP Ultimate Post Grid, Formidable Forms, GoodLayers, and Slider Revolution
See the likely source and whether it is active, inactive, or no longer installed
Identify possible orphaned options using cautious ownership matching
Disable autoload without deleting the saved option value
Restore the option’s previous autoload state from AssistKit Changes
Keep option values private and protected WordPress options read-only

Administration Tools

Manage WordPress more efficiently with tools designed for website owners and agencies.

Role Access Management
Restrict plugin installation access
Restrict theme appearance access
Hide dashboard widgets
Hide admin notices
Last Login tracking
Last Updated tracking

Performance Optimization

Improve loading speed and Core Web Vitals with tools designed to reduce unnecessary requests and render-blocking resources.

Optimize WooCommerce script loading
Optimize WordPress Heartbeat API
Disable RSS feeds
Disable self pingbacks
Remove unnecessary header bloat
Remove MediaElement
Remove Dashicons stylesheet
Disable WordPress emoji
Disable Gutenberg Scripts

Security Hardening

Reduce attack surface and improve website security with simple one-click controls.

Disable XML-RPC
Hide WordPress version information
Disable author archives
Prevent user enumeration
Hide detailed login errors
Disable application passwords
Disable comments globally
Add common security headers
Restrict public REST API access with compatibility exceptions
Prevent code execution in the public ‘Uploads’ folder
Disable directory browsing
Protect sensitive files

Design Tweaks

Polish small WordPress interface details for cleaner client and business websites.

Hide the login language selector
Enable infinite scrolling in the Media Library
Disable the block-based widget editor
Hide the frontend admin bar for non-admin users
Link the login logo to the site homepage
Replace the login page WordPress logo with a custom Media Library image
Remove the WordPress logo from the admin bar
Clean the default WordPress admin footer text

Perfect For

WordPress maintenance providers
Freelance web designers
Digital marketing agencies
WooCommerce stores
Membership websites
Business websites
Bloggers and publishers

Lightweight by Design

AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit focuses on practical performance, security, and maintenance improvements without adding unnecessary complexity or excessive server overhead.

Feedback or Support

Need help configuring AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit?

Documentation: AssistKit documentation

Website: WPAssist
sections.installation:
Upload the plugin through Plugins → Add New.
Activate the plugin.
Select AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit from the WordPress admin menu.
Enable the optimization, security, and maintenance features you wish to use.
Save your settings.
sections.faq:
Does AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit improve Core Web Vitals?

Many features are specifically designed to improve performance metrics such as LCP, INP, and overall page loading speed.

Can I enable only the features I need?

Yes. Most optimization features can be enabled or disabled independently.

Does this plugin work with Elementor?

Yes. AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit works alongside Elementor, Divi, Gutenberg, Beaver Builder, and most modern WordPress themes.

Does this plugin work with WooCommerce?

Yes. The plugin includes WooCommerce-specific performance optimizations. If Restrict Public REST API is enabled, AssistKit keeps WooCommerce REST and Store API route prefixes available when WooCommerce is active so carts, checkout, blocks, mobile apps, and integrations are less likely to break.

Is AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit suitable for agencies?

Yes. Role Access Management, maintenance controls, and administration tools make it particularly useful for agencies managing multiple client websites.

Will Restrict Public REST API break forms or ecommerce?

It can if a plugin depends on public /wp-json/ requests. AssistKit shows a warning before enabling the feature and automatically allows known compatibility route prefixes when related plugins are active, including Contact Form 7, WooCommerce, Jetpack, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Formidable Forms, Fluent Forms, Ninja Forms, Site Kit, Yoast SEO, Rank Math, and All in One SEO. Site owners should still test forms, checkout, blocks, mobile apps, and integrations after enabling it.

Does AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit modify server configuration files?

AssistKit does not write PHP debug constants or automatic update constants to core configuration files. Selected Apache/LiteSpeed security hardening options may add or remove clearly marked rules in .htaccess only when the related setting is changed by an administrator.

Does the Autoloaded Options Manager delete plugin settings?

No. The manager changes only whether a selected option loads automatically on every request. The option value remains in the database, and AssistKit records the previous autoload state so it can be restored from the AssistKit Changes table. Protected WordPress options are not actionable.

Does AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit clean the database automatically?

The database tools run only when initiated or scheduled by an administrator. Retention values and cleanup selections save automatically, and the same saved choices are used for manual and daily optimization. WooCommerce and Scheduled Actions cleanup options appear only when their database tables are detected.
sections.changelog:
3.2.1 – July 31, 2026

  • Moved Scheduled Task Health from System into its own CRON dashboard card and sidebar section with a dedicated clock icon.
  • Added a daily automatic scheduled-task health observation while retaining on-demand checks from the CRON page.
  • Added a collapsed read-only reference table for existing WP-Cron events and active Scheduled Actions, capped at 500 displayed rows for large queues.
  • Moved likely task ownership below each issue heading and changed unknown ownership to the clearer “Owner: Unknown” label.
  • Added ownership recognition for updraftplus_ and flamingo_ hooks.
  • Added Dashboard as the first internal sidebar link.
  • Removed the Settings and Role Access submenu links while keeping both screens available from the AssistKit dashboard and sidebar.
  • Generalized abandoned WP-Cron detection so recurring events with no callable callback across three separate daily checks are flagged even when the owning plugin is unknown.
  • Distinguished missing callbacks from registered-but-not-callable callbacks using the WordPress hook registry and is_callable().
  • Migrated the legacy wpa_database_optimization_event to the current AssistKit database optimization hook.
  • Corrected the hidden Role Access screen registration so the dashboard and sidebar links remain accessible without restoring WordPress submenu entries.

3.2.0 – July 31, 2026

  • Added a focused Scheduled Task Health manager that hides healthy tasks and reports only meaningful WP-Cron and Action Scheduler problems.
  • Added detection for repeated Scheduled Action failures, stalled and long-overdue actions, high-confidence duplicate schedules, queue overload, and strong possibly abandoned WP-Cron candidates.
  • Added issue-specific cleanup controls for duplicate or abandoned WP-Cron events, failed action history, and selected stalled, overdue, or duplicate Scheduled Actions.
  • Added best-effort undo for recent WP-Cron removals and kept WordPress core duplicate schedules read-only.
  • Added a read-only Scheduled Task Health summary to Diagnostics Centre.
  • Expanded autoload option ownership recognition for Really Simple Security, Brainstorm Force plugins, Divi Google Fonts, All-in-One WP Migration, Google Site Kit, ShortPixel, and additional Slider Revolution options.
  • Added cleanup of a stale legacy _transient_dirsize_cache row without a valid expiration on WordPress 6.4 or newer.

3.1.8 – July 23, 2026

  • Changed completed Scheduled Action cleanup from 31 days to 15 days.
  • Changed canceled Scheduled Action cleanup from 31 days to 15 days.
  • Changed optional failed Scheduled Action cleanup from 90 days to 60 days.
  • Added dedicated inline SVG icons to the eight main dashboard cards for faster visual navigation.

3.1.7 – July 23, 2026

  • Improved cleanup-selection saving so it does not depend on a second WooCommerce or Action Scheduler table-detection query during the AJAX request.
  • Added post-save verification to avoid false save errors when database filters or persistent caches return an unchanged update result.
  • Added an accessible HTML backup confirmation dialog before manual database optimization runs.
  • Added the same backup confirmation before the daily database optimization schedule is enabled.
  • Reverts the schedule switch when saving fails so the interface always reflects the stored setting.

3.1.6 – July 20, 2026

  • Consolidated the four Database settings cards into one full-width Database Optimization panel.
  • Kept post revision, trash, and auto-draft retention values autosaving when their fields lose focus.
  • Added autosaving cleanup selections shared by manual and daily database optimization.
  • Added conditional WooCommerce cleanup for expired sessions, expired transients, orphaned order items, orphaned item metadata, HPOS addresses, and HPOS operational data.
  • Added conditional Action Scheduler cleanup for old completed and canceled actions, optional old failed actions, and orphaned action logs.
  • Added conservative WooCommerce parent checks against both legacy WordPress order records and HPOS order storage.
  • Added batched cleanup limits and preserved failed Scheduled Actions as disabled by default.
  • Updated the database cleanup progress overlay and last-run summary for the expanded cleanup categories.

3.1.5 – July 18, 2026

  • Improved installed-source matching by including plugin and theme display-name identifiers.
  • Added bounded detection for dynamically constructed option names that use distinctive namespace prefixes.
  • Added WPCode ownership recognition, including legacy plugin identifiers.
  • Expanded Divi and Elegant Themes recognition for et_builder_, et_builder, et_pb_, and et_pb option families.
  • Updated the ownership scan cache schema so previously unresolved options are analyzed again.

3.1.4 – July 18, 2026

  • Fixed WordPress and third-party admin notices appearing inside the AssistKit dashboard banner.
  • Split PHP and WordPress memory limits into separate diagnostic cards.
  • Split upload and POST size limits into separate diagnostic cards.
  • Split maximum execution time, maximum input time, and maximum input variables into separate diagnostic cards with individual guidance.
  • Expanded autoload option ownership recognition for The Events Calendar, Event Tickets, GiveWP, WP Ultimate Post Grid, Formidable Forms, GoodLayers Core and Infinite, and Slider Revolution.

3.1.3 – July 18, 2026

  • Added limited installed-code scanning for up to the 50 largest manageable autoloaded options.
  • Added high-confidence ownership matches from direct option definitions and WordPress Options API references in plugin, MU-plugin, and theme PHP files.
  • Excluded dependency, SDK, test, language, asset, build, and cache directories from ownership scans and added file-size, file-count, and time limits.
  • Added cached, incremental scan results so newly visible table rows can be analyzed without repeating the complete scan.
  • Added an AJAX loading animation while the autoload table and ownership analysis are prepared.

3.1.2 – July 18, 2026

  • Added a curated ownership registry for exact option names and distinctive plugin prefixes.
  • Added high, medium, and low confidence levels for source ownership matches.
  • Added active, inactive, not-installed, must-use plugin, theme, and shared-framework source checks.
  • Added Possible orphan assessments only when a high-confidence owner is recognized but no matching source is installed.
  • Added Freemius SDK detection so shared fs_accounts data is not treated as orphaned while a Freemius-powered plugin is present.
  • Added initial signatures for common ecommerce, SEO, analytics, caching, security, forms, builder, and utility plugins.
  • Kept ambiguous short prefixes advisory so values such as et_, rg_, acf_, woo_, rocket_, and wpb_ do not create unsupported orphan claims.

3.1.1 – July 18, 2026

  • Added an Autoloaded Options Manager to the Database tab.
  • Added an autoload summary showing total, manageable, protected/internal, and WordPress Site Health threshold sizes.
  • Added a top-20 table limited to currently autoloaded, non-protected options.
  • Added likely plugin ownership hints and review assessments without exposing option values.
  • Added reversible Disable Autoload and Re-enable Autoload actions with the original state stored in a non-autoloaded AssistKit change log.
  • Added a collapsed informational table for large protected WordPress options with no modification controls.

3.1.0 – July 11, 2026

  • Added a separate Diagnostics Centre with read-only checks grouped into Site Configuration, Connectivity, Updates & Scheduling, and Performance Environment.
  • Added WordPress Site Health-based tests for REST API availability, loopback requests, WordPress.org communication, background updates, scheduled events, page cache, persistent object cache, and database server compatibility.
  • Added AssistKit-specific diagnostics for WordPress/Site Address differences, HTTPS, search visibility, environment type, debug configuration, outbound HTTP restrictions, WP-Cron configuration, recorded update failures, memory limits, upload limits, and execution limits.
  • Added clear Good, Informational, Recommended, Critical, and Unavailable statuses with expandable technical details and cached results.
  • Added WordPress 6.0-compatible fallback detection for page caching and persistent object caching.

3.0.14 – July 7, 2026

  • Confirmed uninstall cleanup does not include a survey or external feedback flow.
  • Added a database cleanup progress overlay for manual cleanup runs.
  • Added clickable plugin and theme auto-update status pills with review and disable controls.
  • Updated the Update Management Status card to use a two-column desktop grid and one column on mobile.

  • Updated stored option names from legacy short-prefix keys to AssistKit-prefixed keys for WordPress.org compliance.
  • Added automatic migration from legacy settings keys to the new AssistKit option names.
  • Renamed remaining plugin method callbacks and admin identifiers to use the AssistKit prefix.

  • Addressed WordPress.org review feedback with additional prefix cleanup for classes, constants, AJAX actions, script handles, and scheduled events.
